Name: NIST SP 1500-1r2 — NIST Big Data Interoperability Framework, Volume 1: Definitions (2019)
Why it is useful: The definition of big data used in Lesson 1, by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Name: NIST FIPS 180-4 — Secure Hash Standard
Why it is useful: The official standard that defines SHA-256, the hash function of Lesson 3.

Name: NIST IR 8202 — Blockchain Technology Overview (2018)
Why it is useful: A neutral overview of how blockchains work and when they are used; good background reading for Lessons 3 and 4.

Name: EDPB Guidelines 02/2025 on processing of personal data through blockchain technologies (version 2.0, adopted 7 July 2026)
Why it is useful: The European Data Protection Board on blockchains and personal data (GDPR); Lesson 3, the price of a blockchain.

Name: Dean and Ghemawat (2004), MapReduce: Simplified Data Processing on Large Clusters, OSDI '04
Why it is useful: The Google paper that introduced MapReduce; Lesson 1.

Name: Nakamoto (2008), Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
Why it is useful: The nine-page paper that describes the first blockchain, its hash chain and proof of work; Lessons 3 and 4.

Name: Wüst and Gervais (2018), Do you need a Blockchain? (IACR ePrint 2017/375, CC BY)
Why it is useful: The decision flowchart of Lesson 4 is adapted from this paper (licence: Creative Commons Attribution).

Name: Apache Software Foundation
Why it is useful: The non-profit foundation behind Spark, Parquet and Hadoop.

Name: Apache Spark
Why it is useful: The distributed processing engine of Lesson 2; version 4.3.0 was released on 30 October 2026.

Name: Apache Parquet
Why it is useful: The open columnar file format of Lesson 2, with its specification.

Name: Apache Hadoop
Why it is useful: The open-source MapReduce and HDFS project of Lesson 1.

Name: DuckDB
Why it is useful: The analytical database of our studio; version 2.0.1 is current (November 2026).

Name: DuckDB 2.0.0 announcement (21 October 2026)
Why it is useful: What changed in DuckDB 2.0, including the storage-format note.

Name: Python hashlib documentation
Why it is useful: The standard-library module used for SHA-256 in Examples 3 and in Lab 2.

Name: Bitcoin
Why it is useful: The first public, permissionless blockchain (network launched in January 2009).

Name: Ethereum — The Merge
Why it is useful: Ethereum's move from proof of work to proof of stake on 15 September 2022 (about 99.95 % less energy).

Name: Ethereum — Introduction to smart contracts
Why it is useful: Programs stored on a blockchain; Lesson 4, subtopic 3.

Name: Hyperledger Fabric (LF Decentralized Trust)
Why it is useful: An open-source permissioned blockchain platform for business networks; Lesson 4.

Name: Open Source Initiative — approved licences
Why it is useful: Where to check that a tool is really open source.

Name: Databricks — What is Parquet?
Why it is useful: A vendor page with a published CSV-versus-Parquet comparison on 1 TB of data (87 % less storage).

Name: Microsoft Learn — Data virtualization guide (SQL Server)
Why it is useful: How SQL Server 2022 and 2025 read CSV and Parquet files (the SQL Server note of Lesson 2).

Name: VirusTotal — scan a URL
Why it is useful: Check any address before you open it; a clean result is never a guarantee.

Name: Google Safe Browsing — site status
Why it is useful: A second opinion on a domain.
